Daily Quiz.question: ১) Which one is not related to Shakespeare?
Daily Quiz.exp: Cristopher Marlowe is called the father of tragedy. The rests are related to Shakespeare. William Shakespeare, Shakespeare also spelled Shakspere, byname Bard of Avon or Swan of Avon, (baptized April 26, 1564, Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, England—died April 23, 1616, Stratford-upon-Avon), English poet, dramatist, and actor often called the English national poet and considered by many to be the greatest dramatist of all time. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare

৩) Who wrote ‘Double Falsehood’?
Daily Quiz.exp: In collaboration with John Fletecher and Lewis Theobald, William Shakespeare wrote Double Falsehood.

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) When did Shakespeare write and performed for the first time the play ‘The Tempest’?
Daily Quiz.exp: The Tempest, drama in five acts by William Shakespeare, first written and performed about 1611 and published in the First Folio of 1623. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Tempest

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Shakespeare is known as-
Daily Quiz.exp: Shakespeare is known as Elizabthan Dramatist although he wrote some of his play at the Jacobean Period. Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) When did Shakespeare first appear in the Literary World?
Daily Quiz.exp: The first reference to Shakespeare in the literary world of London comes in 1592, when a fellow dramatist, Robert Greene, declared in a pamphlet written on his deathbed. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) Othello, a famous tragedy written by Shakespeare is known as-
Daily Quiz.exp: Othello, in full Othello, the Moor of Venice, tragedy in five acts by William Shakespeare, written in 1603–04 and published in 1622 in a quarto edition from a transcript of an authorial manuscript. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Othello-by-Shakespeare

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) ‘Benedick’- is character from which Shakespeare’s play?
Daily Quiz.exp: The character Benedick taken from-  Much Ado About Nothing. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/list-of-characters-in-plays-by-Shakespeare-2069474

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) Shakespeare died at-
Daily Quiz.exp: On April 23, 1616, English poet and playwright William Shakespeare died in his hometown of Stratford-upon-Avon at the age of fifty-two. Source: https://www.britannica.com/story/400th-anniversary-of-shakespeares-death

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) Which one is Shakespeare’s poem?
Daily Quiz.option2: খ) The Phoenix and the Turtle
Daily Quiz.exp: All of the above poems are written by Shakespeare. Source: https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) When Shakespeare’s 154 sonnets that were first published all together in a quarto?
Daily Quiz.exp: The publication of drama in the early 17th century was usually left to the poorer members of the Stationers’ Company (which issued licenses) and to outright pirates. The would-be publisher had only to get hold of a manuscript, by fair means or foul, enter it as his copy (or dispense with the formality), and have it printed. Such a man was Thomas Thorpe, the publisher of Shakespeare’s sonnets (1609). The mysterious “Mr. W.H.” in the dedication is thought by some to be the person who procured him his copy. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Shakespeare-on-Theatre-1371445

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) Which one is the compilation of Shakespeare’s work?
Daily Quiz.exp: First Folio, first published edition (1623) of the collected works of William Shakespeare, originally published as Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories & Tragedies. It is the major source for contemporary texts of his plays. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/First-Folio

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) “Petrochio’ - is a character taken from which play?
Daily Quiz.option1: ক) The Taming of the Shrew
Daily Quiz.exp: This character is taken from - The Taming of the Shrew. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/list-of-characters-in-plays-by-Shakespeare-2069474

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) From which Shakespeare’s play the character ‘Wired Sisters’- is taken from?
Daily Quiz.exp: Weird Sisters, also called Three Witches, the creatures who prophesy the destinies of the main characters in Shakespeare’s Macbeth. The term Weird Sisters was first used by Scots writers as a sobriquet for the Fates of Greek and Roman mythology. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Weird-Sisters

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Which one is not a tragedy?
Daily Quiz.exp: The Winter’s Tale is a romantic comedy and the rests of the play are tragedy. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/list-of-plays-by-Shakespeare-2069685

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) ‘King Ferdinand” is a character taken from which play?
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Merry Wives of Windsor
Daily Quiz.exp: The play opens as Ferdinand, the king of Navarre, and three of his noblemen—Berowne (Biron), Longaville, and Dumaine (Dumain)—debate their intellectual intentions. Their plans are thrown into disarray, however, when the Princess of France, attended by three ladies (Rosaline, Maria, and Katharine), arrives on a diplomatic mission from the king of France and must therefore be admitted into Navarre’s park. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Loves-Labours-Lost-by-Shakespeare

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) Which one is a dark comedy?
Daily Quiz.option2: খ) The Merry Wives of Windsor
Daily Quiz.exp: Measure for Measure, a “dark” comedy in five acts by William Shakespeare, written about 1603–04 and published in the First Folio of 1623 from a transcript of an authorial draft. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Measure-for-Measure

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) Among all the options, which one is not a chronicle play/ historical play?
Daily Quiz.exp: King Lear is a tragedy. The rest of the options are chronicle plays. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/list-of-plays-by-Shakespeare-2069685

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) ‘Valentine’ is a character from which play?
Daily Quiz.option2: খ) The Merry Wives of Windsor
Daily Quiz.option3: গ) The Two Gentlemen of Verona
Daily Quiz.exp: Valentine (one of the two gentlemen of the title) opens the play by chiding his closest friend, Proteus (the other gentleman), for remaining idly at home with his beloved Julia rather than venturing to Milan with him. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Two-Gentlemen-of-Verona

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) Frailty, thy name is woman.--from which play the quotation is taken from?
Daily Quiz.exp: In his resultant soliloquy, Hamlet denounces his mother's swift remarriage with the statement, ''Frailty, thy name is woman.'' He thus describes all of womankind as frail and weak in character.
